findings.title: unsubscribe action crashes with NoMethodError when no TopicUser record exists
findings.body: In TopicsController#unsubscribe, `tu = TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id])` can return nil (a user who has never interacted with the topic has no TopicUser row). The very next line calls `tu.notification_level`, which raises NoMethodError on nil, producing a 500 error instead of unsubscribing. The code should use `TopicUser.change(current_user.id, params[:topic_id], notification_level: ...)` (which creates the row if missing, as done in #set_notifications) or handle the nil case explicitly.

findings.title: unsubscribe action does not verify the user can see the topic
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe builds `TopicView.new(params[:topic_id], current_user)` but never calls `guardian.ensure_can_see!` on the topic. TopicView.new may raise Discourse::InvalidAccess for inaccessible topics, but the action also mutates the current user's TopicUser notification level before any visibility check is guaranteed, and unlike #show it does not clean up notifications or handle InvalidAccess. A user who cannot see a topic (e.g. a restricted-category topic) can still hit /t/:id/unsubscribe and toggle their notification state for it. The topic should be fetched and `guardian.ensure_can_see!(topic)` called before mutating TopicUser.

findings.title: unsubscribe toggle logic silently does nothing for muted users and mislabels the action
findings.body: The toggle in #unsubscribe is `if tu.notification_level > regular then regular else muted end`. For a user whose level is already `muted` (0), the condition is false, so the level is set to `muted` again — the link never restores notifications for muted users, it only ever mutes or downgrades. Additionally, the email copy says 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic', but for watching/tracking users the action only downgrades to regular (they still get emails), which contradicts the promise in the email and the client-side text 'You will stop receiving notifications'. The intended behavior (mute when above regular, restore to regular when muted) is not implemented.

findings.title: unsubscribe renders the full topic show response, leaking topic content and preloading it
findings.body: After mutating the notification level, #unsubscribe calls `perform_show_response`, which serializes the entire TopicView (all posts the guardian can see) and, for HTML requests, calls `store_preloaded("topic_#{id}", ...)` and renders :show. The unsubscribe endpoint is meant to be a lightweight landing page reached from an email link; rendering the full topic leaks the topic body to anyone with the URL (subject only to normal guardian checks, which are not explicitly performed here) and does heavy work. It should render a minimal confirmation instead of the full topic payload.

findings.title: check_xhr is skipped for unsubscribe, allowing non-XHR state-changing GET
findings.body: `skip_before_filter :check_xhr, only: [:show, :unsubscribe, :feed]` permits the state-changing `unsubscribe` action to be triggered by a plain GET request from any context, including via CSRF-style link prefetching or cross-site /link tags (the endpoint is same-origin but a cross-site GET from a browser is still possible since no CSRF token is required for GET). Combined with the missing visibility check, this makes the notification-level mutation triggerable by simple navigation. A POST/PUT route or an explicit confirmation would be safer.

findings.title: topic-unsubscribe route creates a record in the store that is never cleaned up and fetches data needlessly
findings.body: The route's model hook calls `this.store.createRecord("topic", { id: params.id })`, which inserts a new (unsaved, id-only) Topic record into the Ember Data store, then immediately overwrites it via `topic.updateFromJson(json)` from `PostStream.loadTopicView`. Creating a store record for an id-only object pollutes the identity map (a later real fetch of the same topic id may return this stub), and `loadTopicView` duplicates the normal topic-loading path. The route should use `this.store.find('topic', params.id)` or the standard topic model hook instead of createRecord.

findings.title: afterModel sets a nested property path that Ember cannot observe on a plain object
findings.body: `topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null)` assumes `topic.details` is an Ember object; if `details` is a plain JS object (as serialized topic details typically are in this codebase), setting a nested path on it will not be tracked and may silently fail or throw depending on the Ember version. The intent (hide the notification reason text on the unsubscribe page) is not reliably achieved.

findings.title: Misspelled property name stopNotificiationsText
findings.body: The computed property is named `stopNotificiationsText` (missing the 'a' in 'Notifications'), and the template references `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` so it works, but the misspelling will confuse future maintainers and any external references. It should be renamed to `stopNotificationsText` in both the controller and the template.

findings.title: Triple-stache output of stopNotificiationsText injects the topic title as raw HTML
findings.body: The template renders `{{{stopNotificiationsText}}}` (unescaped). The string is built from `I18n.t("topic.unsubscribe.stop_notifications", { title: this.get("model.fancyTitle") })`. `fancyTitle` is HTML-escaped server-side (ERB::Util.html_escape in Topic#fancy_title), but I18n interpolation does not re-escape, and any locale override or future change to the title source would inject raw HTML into the page. The locale string itself contains `{{title}}`, so the title must be escaped before interpolation (e.g. via `Em.I18n` with escaped params or by escaping in the controller) rather than relying on the server-side escaping surviving the round trip.

findings.title: dropdown-button renderString interpolates unescaped values into HTML (XSS)
findings.body:
renderString builds HTML by string concatenation: `buffer.push("
  • ")` and `buffer.push("" + row.title + "")` etc. None of `id`, `row.title`, `row.description`, `row.styleClasses`, `this.get('text')`, `title`, or `longDescription` are HTML-escaped. Any caller that passes user-controlled data (e.g. topic titles, category names) into dropDownContent/text will produce an XSS vulnerability. The component should escape all interpolated values (e.g. with a Handlebars escape or _.escape) before pushing them into the buffer.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url passed to emails points to a login-required page with no key, so email clients cannot use it
findings.body: `send_notification_email` sets `unsubscribe_url: post.topic.unsubscribe_url`, which is `#{Discourse.base_url}/t/#{slug}/#{id}/unsubscribe`. The TopicsController#unsubscribe action is behind `ensure_logged_in`, so a recipient opening the link from an email (typically not logged in, or in a mail client with no Discourse session) is bounced to the login page and the unsubscribe never happens. Unlike the digest's `@unsubscribe_key` (DigestUnsubscribeKey), there is no per-user token authenticating this URL. Either the route must accept an authenticated key (like email/unsubscribe/:key) or the link must be removed; as shipped the 'stop receiving notifications about this particular topic' link in every notification email is broken for logged-out users.

findings.title: List-Unsubscribe header still points to user preferences, not the per-topic unsubscribe URL
findings.body: In `header_args`, when `add_unsubscribe_link` is set the `List-Unsubscribe` header is set to `<#{template_args[:user_preferences_url]}>` — the generic preferences page — even though the PR adds a per-topic `unsubscribe_url` to template_args. Mail clients that expose a one-click unsubscribe (RFC 2369/8058) will therefore send users to preferences rather than actually unsubscribing from the topic, and the header does not reflect the new per-topic capability. The header should use `template_args[:unsubscribe_url]` when present (falling back to user_preferences_url), and ideally include a `mailto:` alternative per RFC 8058.

findings.title: body appends unsubscribe text unconditionally when add_unsubscribe_link is set, even if body is nil
findings.body: `body` does `body = @opts[:body]` then, when `@opts[:add_unsubscribe_link]` is true, executes `body << "\n"`. If `@opts[:body]` is nil (callers that rely on a template, e.g. `template: 'user_notifications.signup'`, pass no :body), this raises NoMethodError on nil. The guard should check that body is present (or initialize it to a String) before appending.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link placeholder only substituted in html_part, not in the plain-text body template
findings.body: The HTML email template now contains `%{unsubscribe_link}`, and `html_part` substitutes it via `html_override.gsub!("%{unsubscribe_link}", ...)`. However the plain-text path (`MessageBuilder#body`) appends `I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args)` directly, which is fine, but any other HTML template that contains `%{unsubscribe_link}` and is rendered through a path that does not go through `html_part`'s gsub (or templates rendered before this change) will leak the literal `%{unsubscribe_link}` placeholder to recipients. The substitution should be centralized so both HTML and text bodies get the placeholder replaced consistently.

findings.title: unsubscribe_link locale string promises per-topic unsubscribe that requires login
findings.body: The new locale text says 'To stop receiving notifications about this particular topic, [click here](%{unsubscribe_url}).' but the target URL requires an authenticated session (see TopicsController#unsubscribe ensure_logged_in) and has no per-user token, so recipients opening it from email are redirected to login and the promised action does not occur. The copy overpromises; either fix the endpoint to work logged-out (token-based) or reword the copy.

findings.title: No test verifies the per-topic unsubscribe_url appears in the email body or List-Unsubscribe header
findings.body: The spec adds `unsubscribe_url: "/t/1234/unsubscribe"` to the builder under test but only asserts that the List-Unsubscribe header is present and that the body contains the user_preferences_url. Nothing asserts that the body contains the per-topic unsubscribe URL (via the updated `unsubscribe_link` locale string) nor that the List-Unsubscribe header uses it. The core behavior of this PR — the per-topic unsubscribe link in notification emails — is untested, and the header assertion would still pass with the old preferences-only header.

findings.title: No controller/request specs for the new unsubscribe endpoint
findings.body: The PR adds a new `unsubscribe` action and two new routes (`t/:slug/:topic_id/unsubscribe`, `t/:topic_id/unsubscribe`) but includes no specs covering: the nil TopicUser case, the toggle behavior for muted vs watching users, the slug-mismatch 301 redirect, the login requirement, or the response format. Given the endpoint mutates notification state and is linked from every notification email, request specs are needed before merge.

findings.title: topicUnsubscribe route is registered as a top-level route instead of nested under the topic resource
findings.body: `this.route('topicUnsubscribe', { path: '/t/:slug/:id/unsubscribe' })` is declared outside the `this.resource('topic', ...)` block, so it does not inherit the topic resource's model/controller context. The route's model hook therefore cannot use `this.modelFor('topic')` and must re-fetch the topic itself (which it does via createRecord/loadTopicView). Nesting it under the topic resource (`this.route('unsubscribe', { path: '/unsubscribe' })` inside the resource) would give it the parent topic model for free and match the server route structure.

findings.title: unsubscribe_url uses url (absolute) but is named like relative_url and is interpolated into emails inconsistently
findings.body: `unsubscribe_url` is defined as `"#{url}/unsubscribe"` where `url` is the absolute URL (`Discourse.base_url`-prefixed, see Topic.url). It is passed to the mailer as `unsubscribe_url` and interpolated into the locale string, which is correct for emails, but the name suggests a relative URL like `relative_url`. More importantly, `Topic#url` appends a post number only when > 1, so this is fine, but any caller expecting a path (e.g. for a redirect) would get an absolute URL. The naming should be clarified (e.g. keep it but document it is absolute) to avoid misuse.

findings.title: CSS override `bottom: initial` is invalid and does not achieve the intended dropdown positioning
findings.body: The new `.topic-unsubscribe .notification-options .dropdown-menu { bottom: initial; }` uses `initial` as a value for `bottom`. `initial` resets a property to its initial value, which for `bottom` is `auto` — but the intent appears to be to stop the dropdown menu from being positioned above the button (the notification-options component normally uses `bottom: 100%`-style drop-up styling). `bottom: initial`/`auto` will not reliably produce the desired drop-down behavior across browsers and likely leaves the menu mispositioned on the unsubscribe page. The rule should be verified against the actual notification-options markup and given an explicit value.
